images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ τοῖς πολίταις διαλέγεται· ὁ δὲ Χαιρεφῶν ἀκούει.
images.alt_en: The Athenian Agora in the morning: Socrates, barefoot, snub-nosed, in a plain cloak, talks with a group of citizens under a plane tree; his thin, excitable friend Chaerephon listens beside him, leaning forward.

images.alt_grc: ἡ Πυθία ἐπὶ τοῦ τρίποδος καθημένη τῷ Χαιρεφῶντι ἀναιρεῖ.
images.alt_en: Inside the temple of Apollo at Delphi: the Pythia, a woman in a white robe and laurel wreath, sits on a tall bronze tripod holding a laurel sprig and a shallow bowl; Chaerephon stands before her, asking his question.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης τὸν πολιτικὸν ἐλέγχει· οἱ δὲ παρόντες ὀργίζονται.
images.alt_en: In a colonnade of the Agora Socrates questions a well-dressed politician, who looks flustered; the politician's friends glare at Socrates, while young men behind him grin.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Αἰγεὺς τὸν θεὸν ἐν Δελφοῖς ἐρωτᾷ.
images.alt_en: Attic red-figure cup by the Kodros Painter, c. 440–430 BC (Berlin, Antikensammlung F 2538): King Aegeus consults the Delphic prophetess, labelled Themis, who sits on Apollo's tripod (museum object, photograph CC).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Εὐθύφρων τῷ Σωκράτει πρὸ τῆς τοῦ βασιλέως στοᾶς ἐντυγχάνει.
images.alt_en: Morning in the north-west corner of the Agora, 399 BC: in front of a small Doric colonnade (the King's Porch) the grey-bearded Socrates waits; Euthyphro, a self-important seer in a fine cloak, hurries up to greet him in surprise.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Μέλητος, νέος τις καὶ ἀγνώς, τὴν γραφὴν ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τίθησιν.
images.alt_en: Inside the colonnade: a young man with lank hair, a thin beard and a hooked nose (Meletus) hands a written charge to the King Archon's clerk; a notice board with whitened tablets behind them.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Εὐθύφρων σπεύδει· ὁ δὲ Σωκράτης μόνος ἀπορεῖ.
images.alt_en: Euthyphro hurrying off across the Agora with his cloak flapping, glancing back; Socrates stands alone by the porch, one hand on his chin, still puzzling.

images.alt_grc: ἡ τοῦ βασιλέως στοὰ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ.
images.alt_en: The foundations of the Stoa Basileios (the King's Porch) in the Athenian Agora, excavated in 1970, with the Hephaisteion on the hill behind (site photograph, CC).

images.alt_grc: πρῲ ὁ Σωκράτης εἰς τὸ γυμνάσιον ἔρχεται· πληθούσης δὲ τῆς ἀγορᾶς ἐκεῖ φανερός ἐστιν.
images.alt_en: A split scene: left, early morning at a gymnasium outside the walls, youths exercising under plane trees while Socrates walks and talks in a covered walk; right, the Agora full of stalls and shoppers at mid-morning, Socrates in the middle of a small crowd.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης ἐρωτᾷ· τί δίκαιον, τί ἄδικον; οἱ δὲ νεανίαι ἀκούουσιν.
images.alt_en: Socrates sits on a stone bench in a colonnade, counting questions on his fingers; around him young men listen, one of them (young Xenophon, a horseman's riding boots on) taking notes on a wax tablet.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Εὐθύδημος πολλὰ βιβλία ἔχει· ὁ δὲ Σωκράτης αὐτὸν ἐρωτᾷ.
images.alt_en: A saddler's shop near the Agora where young men gather: the proud young Euthydemus holding an armful of papyrus rolls; Socrates questions him; in an inset, the words ΓΝΩΘΙ ΣΑΥΤΟΝ carved on a temple wall at Delphi.

images.alt_grc: γνῶθι σαυτόν.
images.alt_en: Roman floor mosaic of a reclining skeleton beside the Greek words ΓΝΩΘΙ ΣΑΥΤΟΝ, 'know yourself', 1st–3rd century AD (Rome, Museo Nazionale Romano; museum object, photograph CC).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Μένων τὸν ἀκόλουθον καλεῖ· ὁ δὲ Σωκράτης ἐν τῇ ψάμμῳ γράφει.
images.alt_en: A courtyard in Athens, about 402 BC: the elegant young Thessalian Meno, richly dressed, beckons one of his many attendants, a boy of about twelve; Socrates squats beside a patch of smooth sand with a stick.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης τετράγωνον χωρίον γράφει· ὁ δὲ παῖς ἀποκρίνεται.
images.alt_en: Close-up: a square drawn in the sand, each side marked '2', divided into four smaller squares; Socrates points with his stick while the slave boy, barefoot, counts on his fingers; Meno watches with folded arms.

images.alt_grc: ὁ παῖς οἴεται τὴν γραμμὴν διπλασίαν εἶναι· ὁ δὲ Σωκράτης πρὸς τὸν Μένωνα βλέπει.
images.alt_en: The boy confidently draws a much larger square with doubled sides (4 × 4), far too big; Socrates turns to Meno with a raised eyebrow; in a faint inset, the correct figure: a square drawn on the diagonal of the first.

images.alt_grc: ἡ Ἀκαδήμεια ἡ τοῦ Πλάτωνος.
images.alt_en: The archaeological site of Plato's Academy in Athens: stone foundations among olive and plane trees in the park of Akadimia Platonos (site photograph, CC).

images.alt_grc: ὁ ποιμὴν εἰς τὸ χάσμα καταβαίνει καὶ ἵππον χαλκοῦν ὁρᾷ.
images.alt_en: Lydia after a storm: a shepherd climbs down into a fresh crack in the hillside; inside, a huge hollow bronze horse with little doors, and through one of them the pale body of a giant with a gold ring on his finger. Sheep peer over the edge above.

images.alt_grc: ὁ ποιμὴν τὴν σφενδόνην στρέφει καὶ ἀφανὴς γίγνεται.
images.alt_en: The shepherds' monthly meeting before the king's steward: the shepherd sits among the others, turning the ring's bezel into his palm; his outline is fading to nothing while the man next to him talks as if he had gone.

images.alt_grc: ὁ δίκαιος καὶ ὁ ἄδικος δακτυλίους ἔχουσιν.
images.alt_en: Two men with identical gold rings stand at the edge of a crowded market, both half-invisible, both reaching toward a table of silver and fine goods; Socrates and Glaucon watch from a bench, Glaucon gesturing.

images.alt_grc: νόμισμα Λυδικόν.
images.alt_en: An early electrum coin of Lydia with a lion's head, about 600 BC: Lydia, the kingdom of Gyges, is where coins were first struck (museum object, CC0).

images.alt_grc: ὁ δακτύλιος
images.alt_en: A gold finger ring with an engraved stone.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κρίτων τὸν παῖδα πέμπει· ὁ δὲ ἄνθρωπος τὸ φάρμακον ἐν κύλικι φέρει.
images.alt_en: The prison cell at sunset, light slanting through a small high window: Socrates, just bathed, sits on his bed among his friends; grey-haired Crito nods to a slave boy at the door, and a quiet official enters carrying a plain cup.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης τὴν κύλικα λαμβάνει καὶ εὐκόλως ἐκπίνει.
images.alt_en: Socrates, calm and upright, takes the cup from the official and looks at him from under his brows; the official explains with a gesture toward his own legs; the friends around them freeze.

images.alt_grc: οἱ φίλοι δακρύουσιν· ὁ δὲ Σωκράτης· ἡσυχίαν ἄγετε.
images.alt_en: The friends weeping: young Phaedo covering his face with his cloak, Crito standing up to leave, Apollodorus sobbing aloud; Socrates, walking slowly about the room, raises a hand to quiet them.

images.alt_grc: τὸ κώνειον.
images.alt_en: Poison hemlock (Conium maculatum), the plant from which the Athenian κώνειον was prepared: white umbrella-shaped flowers and purple-spotted stems (plant photograph, CC).

images.alt_grc: ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Σωκράτους πιέζει.
images.alt_en: Socrates lies on his back on the prison bed, his face covered with his cloak; the official presses his foot and asks if he can feel it; his friends watch in silence.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης ἐκκαλυψάμενος· ὦ Κρίτων, τῷ Ἀσκληπιῷ ὀφείλομεν ἀλεκτρυόνα.
images.alt_en: Socrates has uncovered his face and turns his head toward Crito, who leans close; in the shadows of the cell a small votive image of Asclepius with his snake-staff; outside the window, a cock on a wall.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κρίτων τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ Σωκράτους συλλαμβάνει.
images.alt_en: Crito gently closes Socrates' eyes and mouth; the friends stand around the bed, heads bowed; the empty cup on the floor.

images.alt_grc: ὁ τοῦ Σωκράτους θάνατος.
images.alt_en: Jacques-Louis David, The Death of Socrates, 1787, oil on canvas (New York, Metropolitan Museum of Art 31.45; public domain, CC0).
